questions: Should the plot be cleared before drawing (e.g., plt.clf()) to avoid overlapping with previous plots, or is it acceptable to draw on the current figure?
Should the function set any plot title, axis labels, or other formatting beyond legend and grid?
Is the x-axis range for the plot determined solely by the input array x, or should the function adjust axis limits (e.g., plt.xlim) automatically?
Should the function handle complex-valued input arrays x, or is x assumed to be real-valued?
If the input array x contains NaN or Inf values, should the function propagate them through norm.pdf, handle them specially, or raise an error?
Should the function ensure the plot window is displayed (plt.show()) and block execution until closed, or return immediately after calling show?
Is the function expected to work with scalar inputs (converted to array), or only strictly with numpy.ndarray as per type check?
Should the function validate that x is a 1-D array, or can it handle multi-dimensional arrays and compute distributions per dimension?
